name: Neco
title: Egypt's Pharaoh who killed King Josiah
summary: Neco II (also called Pharaoh Neco) was an Egyptian pharaoh of the 26th dynasty who played a significant role in Judah's final days. He is best known for killing the righteous King Josiah at the Battle of Megiddo, and for deposing Josiah's son Jehoahaz and installing Jehoiakim as a vassal king over Judah.

keyEvents.title: Neco marches through Judah toward Assyria
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh Neco marched up against the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah attempted to stop him at Megiddo.

keyEvents.title: The killing of King Josiah at Megiddo
keyEvents.description: Despite Neco's warning that he had no quarrel with Judah, Josiah went into battle against him and was mortally wounded at Megiddo.

keyEvents.title: The deposition of King Jehoahaz
keyEvents.description: After only three months on the throne, Neco deposed Josiah's son Jehoahaz as king over Judah and took him captive to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: The Installation of Jehoiakim as Vassal King
keyEvents.description: Necho installed Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim as king over Judah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He imposed a heavy tax of silver and gold on the land.

keyEvents.title: Necho's Defeat at Carchemish
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh Necho suffered a decisive defeat against Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Carchemish, marking the end of Egypt's influence in the region.
